key_insight: A locally deployable small language model can support end-to-end genomic variant interpretation, including ACMG criterion assignment and trio-based inheritance reasoning, while deterministic code handles the arithmetic and reporting steps.
clinical_relevance: This could enable privacy-preserving variant review on hospital hardware, making advanced genomic interpretation more accessible without sending patient data to the cloud.
method: Benchmarked 13 small language models on 150 multiple-choice genetics questions and selected Qwen3.5-9B.
Built a four-stage IVA pipeline that assigns ACMG/AMP criteria, applies inheritance logic, and generates structured reports.
Used deterministic code for retrieval, phasing, point summation, citation checking, and formatting.
evidence_signal: IVA was evaluated on synthetic scenarios, 16 solved trios, and 327 solved singleton visual impairment cases; it reported all key trio variants, recovered 93% of causative singleton variants, and achieved 81% benchmark accuracy for the chosen small model.
watch_item: Performance remained imperfect, with precision limitations and recurrent errors such as omission, unverified mechanism, label-reasoning mismatch, and arithmetic mistakes.
paper_title: IVA, a locally deployable Intelligent Variant Analyser based on a small language model for complete case-level and trio-based genomic interpretation.
